formats.key: buyArtworks(bytes32 r_,bytes32 s_,uint8 v_,(uint256 price,uint256 cost,uint256 expiryTime,address destination,uint256[] tokenIds,(address recipient,uint256 bps)[][] revenueShares,bool payByVaultContract) saleData_)
effects: Without vault payment: the signer sends msg.value ETH, and the contract requires it to equal saleData_.price.
With vault payment (payByVaultContract=true): the vault pays the price. msg.value is not checked, so any ETH the signer attaches is taken and stays in the contract.
Each artwork in tokenIds goes from the contract to `destination`.
The price is split between the revenue-share recipients (after advances are deducted) and costReceiver. `cost` is a part of the price, not an extra charge.
formats.shown: Purchase artworks for Recipient. The screen shows Price, Platform cost, Recipient, Artworks, Offer expires and "Pay via vault" as raw true/false. The native value is not shown, and the revenue shares do not render.

findings.title: buyArtworks has no @.value field, and in vault mode nothing ties the ETH sent to the Price shown.
findings.evidence: FeralfileArtworkV4_1.buyArtworks: `saleData_.payByVaultContract ? vault.payForSale(r_, s_, v_, saleData_) : require(saleData_.price == msg.value, ...)`. The vault branch does not check msg.value, and leftOver = price - distributedRevenue leaves any extra ETH in the contract. The descriptor has no `@.value` field, and the Price field shows saleData_.price.
findings.fix: Add a field {"path": "@.value", "label": "You pay", "format": "amount"} and put it in the interpolated intent: "Buy artworks for {saleData_.destination} paying {@.value}".

findings.title: buyArtworks label "Platform cost" reads like a fee on top of Price, but it is part of Price.
findings.evidence: FeralfileArtworkV4_1.buyArtworks: itemRevenue = (price - cost) / tokenIds.length; leftOver = price - distributedRevenue goes to costReceiver. Case 6 shows Price 0.5 ETH and Platform cost 0.05 ETH, with msg.value 0.5 ETH.
findings.fix: Change the label to "Platform share (included in price)", or hide the field.

findings.title: buyArtworks interpolated intent leaves out the price the signer pays.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "interpolatedIntent": "Buy artworks for {saleData_.destination}"; case 6 shows "Buy artworks for Receiver".

findings.title: buyArtworks shows "Pay via vault" as a raw true/false with no meaning.
findings.evidence: descriptor field saleData_.payByVaultContract uses format raw; case 6 shows "Pay via vault: false". When it is true, the vault pays and the signer should send no ETH.
findings.fix: Map the bool with an enum: true = "Paid by Feral File vault", false = "Paid by you".

findings.title: buyArtworks test case would revert: revenueShares is empty and the expiry is past.
findings.evidence: In the case 6 calldata, tokenIds = [1001] and revenueShares has length 0. FeralfileSaleData.validateSaleData requires tokenIds.length == revenueShares.length and expiryTime > block.timestamp (expiry 2025-01-01).
findings.fix: Add one revenue share per token and a future expiry. Add a case with payByVaultContract=true.

findings.title: buyArtworks revenue share recipients and bps sit in a nested array that runners do not render.
findings.evidence: descriptor fields saleData_.revenueShares.[].[].recipient and .bps; case 6 renders neither. These splits move no extra signer funds.
findings.fix: Waits on runner support for nested arrays.

findings.format: buyArtworks(bytes32 r_,bytes32 s_,uint8 v_,(uint256 price,uint256 cost,uint256 expiryTime,address destination,uint256[] tokenIds,(address recipient,uint256 bps)[][] revenueShares,bool payByVaultContract) saleData_)
findings.title: buyArtworks has no @.value field, and in vault mode nothing ties the ETH sent to the Price shown.
findings.reason: Without the vault, msg.value must equal the Price shown, so that path is covered. With payByVaultContract=true, nothing checks msg.value, so any ETH the signer attaches is accepted. Payouts use saleData_.price, not msg.value, and no withdraw or sweep function exists in the source here, so the extra ETH is either spent on the sale or stuck in the contract, and the screen never shows the amount.
findings.quote: FeralfileArtworkV4_1.sol buyArtworks (inherited by the deployed FeralfileExhibitionV4_4): `external payable` ... `saleData_.payByVaultContract ? vault.payForSale(r_, s_, v_, saleData_) : require(saleData_.price == msg.value, ...)`; payout is `leftOver = saleData_.price - distributedRevenue; payable(costReceiver).transfer(leftOver)`. descriptor.json buyArtworks fields: price, cost, destination, tokenIds, expiryTime, payByVaultContract (raw), revenueShares. There is no @.value.

findings.format: buyArtworks(bytes32 r_,bytes32 s_,uint8 v_,(uint256 price,uint256 cost,uint256 expiryTime,address destination,uint256[] tokenIds,(address recipient,uint256 bps)[][] revenueShares,bool payByVaultContract) saleData_)
findings.title: buyArtworks has no @.value field, and in vault mode nothing ties the ETH sent to the Price shown.
findings.reason: For a successful vault-funded purchase, buyArtworks accepts attached ETH without checking its amount or refunding it; payouts total only saleData_.price. The screen shows the sale price and vault flag, but omits the additional ETH sent by the signer.
findings.quote: contracts/1-0x614d5475fe81ef4b6dd8093b5c73efeee03167e0/src/contracts/FeralfileArtworkV4_1.sol, buyArtworks: `saleData_.payByVaultContract ? vault.payForSale(r_, s_, v_, saleData_) : require(saleData_.price == msg.value, "FeralfileExhibitionV4: invalid payment amount");` and `uint256 leftOver = saleData_.price - distributedRevenue; if (leftOver > 0) { payable(costReceiver).transfer(leftOver); }`. descriptor.json, buyArtworks format: `"intent": "Purchase artworks"`, `{"path": "saleData_.price", "label": "Price", "format": "amount"}` and `{"path": "saleData_.payByVaultContract", "label": "Pay via vault", "format": "raw"}`; its fields contain no `@.value`.
